title: Fresh contradictory QA after bounded transient sourceId repair

evidence: user:private-course is rejected by transient admission before source-byte read
dot/dash/underscore identity crosses transient admission and M3.3 prepare/verify

finding.title: Windows-reserved DOS device sourceIds can PASS transient admission but are unsafe for mandatory M3.3 local materialization
finding.cause: The transient sourceId regex accepts reserved DOS device basenames such as CON, NUL, AUX, PRN, COM1 and LPT1. M3.3 derives local temporary/archive filename components from sourceId, including <sourceId>.source and <sourceId>.json. These names are reserved on Windows even with extensions, so an admitted identity is not safely materializable across the local portable handoff boundary.
finding.contractImpact: Issue #348 requires every transient-PASS sourceId to be both M3.2/M3.3 binding-valid and safely materializable by M3.3. The historical examples are fixed, but another admitted identifier class violates the same cross-contract invariant.
reproduction: transient.build_admission(valid declaration sourceId='CON', exact bytes) yields PASS_TRANSIENT_SOURCE_ADMISSION_V1
Windows CI independently attempts actual M3.3 prepare/verify with sourceId='CON'
